tion of distribution, the opening of new markets and the division of
work in a village, linking it with the agricultural cooperative move-
ment, and should go a step further to the stage where it can be
closely connected with the village bank movement, consumers’ cooper-
ative society, and mutual benefit society.

Compared with the farm village Saemaul Undong, the city com-
munity Saemaul Undong and the factory Saemaul Undong have not
been so active. The shortage of volunteer leaders and the unexplor-
ation of benefit-making projects for common interest, may be counted
as the reason, but the principal problems are the insufficient under-
standing of and the scarcity of enthusiasm for the Saemaul Undong
on the part of intellectuals and people on the leaders' level.

(8) Before anything else, therefore, we should edify some intellec-
tuals so that they should throw away their wrong preoccupation or
prejudice. This movement is not a movement for any particular people
or some people belonging to any particular class but a pan-national
movement.

One thing we should point out in the end is the identification of

--- (p. 676) ---

the Saemaul Undong. We should add science to industry, self-help and cooperation, making it the ideal backbone, inasmuch as the scientific, ation of the Saemaul Undong can make our living rational and our process of production technical.

## II. The Spirit of the Saemaul Undong

(1) The main guiding ideology of the Saemaul Undong is derived from national goals and aspirations, and a wish for national revitalization. In other words, the Saemaul Undong is a movement to build a materialistic and spiritual basis on which the development and progress of the nation can be achieved so that it may lay a foundation for the unified nation-state where every citizen can enjoy political and economic independence as well as social and cultural diversity under his own free-will which integrates all the others into ‘oneness’.
Another important objective of the Saemaul Undong is the eradication of such negative elements as over-reliance on other countries in political and economic matters, the over-widened gap between the rich and the poor, social and cultural injustices and irrationalities, ideological confusion caused by the division of the country, and national idiosyncracy due to the building of a materialistic basis only. In order to revitalize a nation, the spiritual revolution, the building of a spiritual basis, should precede the material revolution, and the building of a materialistic basis.
The basic spiritual element for national revitalization is national self-consciousness which should be constructive, independent, indigenous, creative, and integrative. In short, it is the contemporary idea of ‘democratic conjunction’ which can conjoin the present and the future of Korea. Thus, the idea of modernization can be best understood as the Saemaul spirit of diligence, self-help, and cooperation. That is the reason why the Saemaul Undong is not construed as a mere program for increasing the national income or improving the observable environments, but as a spiritual revolution even though it first began under the banner of the modernization of the rural

--- (p. 677) ---

## II. The Spirit of the Saemaul Undong

community.
The modernization of a country is a way of revitalizing a nation; thus, it means the idealization of the Saemaul Undong. Generally speaking, the problems of modernization, the goals or wishes of new nations, are the establishment of a welfare-state, the implementation of democracy and the building of a nation-state, and these activities may work in an orderly manner or simultaneously. However, these modernization problems create many difficulties in setting up specific objectives, the decision of priority, and the methods of implementation.
The first problem is the conflict between time-shortening and the traditional factors against it. In other words, in order to achieve modernization within a short period of time, the negative factors in the traditional methods of modernization should be removed; otherwise, the time-shortening program should be given up.
The second problem, which is more important than the first, is the matter of priority, that is, which should be done first; the modernization of the physical environments or that of the human being.
The third problem is the matter of method, that is, how to achieve modernization, for it can be done either from the inside or from the outside. Thus, all the three problems have their own difficulties. However, the Saemaul Undong presents a sample model for solving these modernization problems by harmonizing the ideal ‘time’ and ‘space’ with the methods of our own, in a creative, independent, and constructive manner. In other words, the Saemaul Undong not only extracts the motives of time-shortening for modernization from the traditional factors, but also presents a unique way of modernizing man and environment simultaneously through the harmonized progress of the ‘environment-improvement’, the increase of the national income, and the spiritual revolution. It also attempts to harmonize the inner factors with the outer factors through the realization of a co-operative society with the propagation of science and technology.
And, when seen from the process of modernization, Korea should achieve the national objectives imposed upon it by special situations, such as the maintenance of national security and peaceful unification,

--- (p. 678) ---

in addition to the general modernization process of the establishment
of a nation-state, a welfare-state, the industrialization of the whole
country, and the implementation of a true democracy suitable to the
Korean soil. Thus, the Saemaul Undong shows a new way of allevia-
ting these heavy burdens laid in the process of modernization.
(2) This kind of theoretical principles of the Saemaul Undong will
become more clear when some of the main objectives for the modern-
ization of Korea are examined more closely. The main goals of the
modernization of a nation can be classified into somewhat large
categories such as industrialization, democratization, national unifica-
tion, etc., and these objectives seem to have the same process as
that of the three main goals of a new-born nation, that is, democracy,
nationalism, and industrialism.
First, the Saemaul Undong gives us a concrete form of the idea of
industrialization by making industrialization a specific movement as a
means of attaining better living. Thus, the movement of better living
means not only materialistic betterment but also the industrialization of
the country based on the determination of the rural community with the
spiritual revolution of diligence, self-help, and cooperation, awakening
the latent pure-mind of ‘Love for Farming’ and ‘Love for Hometown’,
which revives the old beautiful tradition of 'All live happily together'.
Moreover, the Saemaul Undong provides a means of resolving all
the problems involved in industrialization. In other words, it provides
not only the means for the complete expulsion of poverty but also a
means of narrowing the gap of living standards between the cities and
the rural areas. It also provides a means of setting up the moral and
ethical understanding of the relationship between the employer and
the employee through the factory Saemaul Undong and the urban or
city Saemaul Undong, both of which are based on the revival of the
communal spirit and the spirit of citizenship and fellowship. In short,
the Saemaul Undong is a way of building a nation-state by means of
industrialization; that is, the establishment of a ‘communal industrial
society’ conscious of the general direction combining the present and
the future within the historical tradition of Korean industrialization.

--- (p. 679) ---

## II. The Spirit of the Saemaul Undong

(3) Political democratization is another main goal and direction of the Saemaul Undong. Nowadays, democracy is faced with many difficulties and criticisms in implementing it in many new-born nations. Korea is no exception to this hard reality. In fact, democracy is a rather complicated and delicate theory and system, and it usually requires long experience and favorable soils in order to implant it and see its growth and development. The situations of most of the new-born nations are not ready for its growth. For example, democracy in Korea, with its unique historical background and present situations, is quite different from that of the Western countries in its growth and development. Besides, such unprecedented historical backgrounds as the highly sophisticated ethical authoritarianism and the distorted political culture due to Japanese colonialism, the destruction of the communal life with the introduction of individualism, the over-swaying of internationalism over Korean internal political affairs, and the hostile confrontation between the North and the South due to the division of the country are some of the main obstacles for the development of democracy in Korea. And the social and economic immaturity also plays a vital role in detrimenting the development of democracy. However, with all these obstacles confronting, the Saemaul Undong has survived as an organized, concrete, and humanistic effort to implant and develop Korean democracy.

Through national industrialization, the Saemaul Undong also presents a definite and workable means of satisfying all the economic and social prerequisites for the development of Korean democracy such as the accumulation of wealth, the enlargement of the middle-class, the building of a sound and beneficial welfare-state, etc.

But, in implanting democracy, the most emphasized directions (points) of the Saemaul Undong are the creation of the spirit of a democratic citizen by means of spiritual development, the training of democratic leaders through the democratic process of the Saemaul Undong, and democratic training itself effected in achieving some of the Saemaul projects. And it should be added that the Saemaul Undong revives the traditional spirit of communal life and changes it

--- (p. 680) ---

into a new modern version so that it may open up a new road to a
true local self-government. Thus, by using the Korean culture as a
seed-bed for democracy, the objectives, the development processes,
and the systematic apparatus of the Saemaul Undong are derived from
democratic ideas and systems, and conjoin democratic nationalism with
the necessary conditions for implanting Korean democracy.

(4) Based on the history of traditional nationalism, the Saemaul Undong promises the peaceful unification of the Korean peninsula by overcoming the obstacles which have been dividing the country since 1945, especially the Korean War. Unification is the most important stimulant for national revitalization and the main objective of modernization. Unification is an ultimate goal of the Korean people in order to overcome their tragic fate and agony caused by the division of the country, and it is also a prerequisite to overcoming other obstacles on the way to a welfare-state. Since unification is a matter of life and death for Korea, it should be achieved by peaceful means; therefore, the first step should be a peaceful settlement by making self-defense its main point. The process of unification should also be steady, for it should not be simply a formal nor reactionary unification. It should be one where the divided people become truly united without any heterogeneity nor any ideological differences, so that it can really promise unified national development. Therefore, fostering a strong conviction in the identity of the Korean people, and knowing the historical mission of the country to preserve the national tradition, we should make it a heraldic main force of the unification that leads into a glorious national development. Thus, it is not an exaggeration to say that the Saemaul Undong is the key to the unification of Korea.

(5) The Saemaul Undong presents a model of national development since it demonstrates its superiority in the methods of modernization as it is based on the traditions of national history and since it tries to bring peace to this country as the preconditions of the unification by means of self-defense. The so-called “economic development of socialism” in north Korea is not only a whirlpool of economic failure but also an anti-national heresy which annihilates the traditional

--- (p. 681) ---

Korean culture completely. And the so-called “revolution of south Korea by the proletariats” is also very far from the ideal unification based on the traditions of national history. In short, the Saemaul Undong is the only way to unify the country peacefully, preserving the national heritage and tradition.

Now, the Saemaul Undong is marking a new era; the establishment of a democratic welfare-state which is one of the national goals of the new era, the realization of social justice through the eradication of all social evils and wrongdoings, the development of the national spirit by showing the potential powers of the nation, etc., are not far from the ideals of the Saemaul Undong.

The Saemaul Undong is, in a sense, a new detonator to solidify nationalism which is directly linked with the goals of modernization, such as industrialization, democratization, unification, etc. In short, the Saemaul Undong is the main factor of building the material and spiritual basis for the unification and the development of the country, and it is the pronoun of modernization on its way to the nationalistic unification.

(6) The idea of the Saemaul Undong can be summarized as follows: It can be said that every culture has its own territory and has its own special meanings and interpretations of a ‘village’. Thus, when the idea of a village which has been formed in the minds of the Korean people, is defined in a general sense, two intrinsic qualities seem to appear:

① The village symbolizes an everlasting root of spiritual life connected with the long tradition of ancestor-worship rather than a mere living place.
② The village is not an artificial idea of collection formed in a supernatural sense, but traditionally it is formed geographically as an assimilated thing grown in natural environments.

When these two meanings are put together, in the minds of the Korean people, the traditional idea about a village is the root of the spiritual bond and a resting place for the mind. Thus, it is based on the universal view of the benevolent village, which is somewhat con-

--- (p. 682) ---

nected with the Confucian view of life. In other words, it idealizes a
community where both the inner and the outer sides of the benevolent
village can conjoin for benevolence. The inner side of it means the
world of the mind, and the outer side means the physical world of
the village.
The basic idea of the new community, Saemaul, can be construed
as a new integrated ideology where the traditional meaning of the
village is added to the idea of scientific modernization, and the prac­
tical learning necessary for the formation of a modern country.

### (7) The main idea of the Saemaul Undong in another sense is an
ingenious integration of the transformation toward a benevolent village—
a spiritual transformation and materialistic modernization as an indus­
trial revolution. The guiding spirit of the Saemaul Undong is dili­
gence, self-help, and cooperation. Among the three principle ideas,
cooperation is based on the traditional idea of benevolent village where
acts of kindness and moral justice are overflowing, and the other two,
diligence and self-help, are based on the idea of capitalism necessary
for modernization. Thus, the Saemaul Undong can be construed as a
behaviorism based on the two ideas combined; the behavior of the
patriotic and dedicated leaders of the Saemaul Undong is engrafted on
the psychological structure of the general public of Korean people.
Let us first consider the narrow sense of the grafted-relationship.
The Korean people usually have an unconscious longing for the ben­
evolent village based on human sentiment and righteousness. When we
consider the broader and positive meaning of relationships there is a
release or catharsis of the psychological tensions such as grudges,
discontents, and rancors, the typical psychological phenomena found
in the Korean people in the course of the successful implementation
of the behaviorism of the Saemaul Undong. Throughout the long
history of Korea, the Korean people have experienced lots of grudges
or rancors such as poverty, ignorance, insult, contemptuous treatment,
wars, and rebellions. When they were faced with such things, they
had experienced only psychological defeatism. However, through the
Saemaul Undong, they began to exercise their spiritual strength in

--- (p. 683) ---

## Ⅱ. The Spirit of the Saemaul Undong

facing their fate,
(8) When we consider the relation between the Saemaul Undong and national security, we could not get rid of the idea of defeatism existant until the 1960s, that is, it was a dominant belief that it was impossible for the Korean people to have an economic independence for national self-defense. Following the Nixon doctrine, the U.S. Army stationed in Korea began to withdraw, and they claimed that the stationing of the U.S. Army in Korea was not an obligation but a right according to the mutual defense treaty between the Republic of Korea and the U.S.A.； thus, in 1977, Carter’s withdraw plan began with a one-way notice. In facing this hard reality, the Saemaul Undong has been playing an important role as a spiritual core factor in establishing a self-defense plan from the time of the Nixon doctrine. Under the new determination of the people that “We should defend our own country” stimulated by the new spirit of self-defense policy, the army equipment modernization plan which began in 1971, was a great success, and in 1975, the Korean people could bear all the defense expenses by means of a defense-tax system.
The second army equipment modernization plan should be pushed ahead until 1985 through the Saemaul Undong, because the number of the north Korean army has increased from 400,000 to 700,000, and our G.N.P. cannot be expect more than a 9% increase due to the oil crisis and the economic depression of the world； thus, it is very difficult to achieve the self-defense modernization project in a foreseeable short period of time. Therefore, in order to overcome all the unfavorable conditions for modernizing the army equipment, we should rely on the spirit of the Saemaul Undong—diligence, self-help, and cooperation.
When the international situation around Korea became unfavorable to Russia because of the unexpected compromise among the three super powers, that is, the U.S.A., Japan, and China, Russia exerted her efforts to exercise great influence over north Korea, and as a result there exists a great danger on the Korean peninsula threatening national security. In an atmosphere of such tension, the necessity of making the Saemaul Undong a part of daily life and activity is felt

--- (p. 684) ---

more strongly than ever before.

(9) When we consider the Saemaul Undong in connection with the sense of a new society, the Saemaul Undong which started in 1970 is, in a sense, a social renewal movement on the structure of thought-patterns, which have changed our way of thinking formed and petrified since the Liberation in 1945 after World War II. Before 1970 when the Saemaul Movement began to appear, there were many self-contradictory and negative factors in the value system and some confusions in establishing the true meaning of society because of the indiscriminate introduction of Western culture, especially the Western value system.
The individualism and liberalism of the West were transformed into selfishness and led into defeatism when people were confronted with the traditional social value system of Korea. Thus, when seen from the socialistic point of view, the Saemaul Undong is a movement for the salvation of a decaying society because the negative cynical elements in the past traditional thought-pattern and the indifferent attitude of the people are changed into a positive and rational thought-pattern by the powerful influence of the Saemaul Undong.

(10) When we turn our attention to the Saemaul Undong in connection with the sense of politics, the Saemaul Undong has nothing to do with politics in a narrow sense of the political power. But, when seen from a broad sense, that is, when politics is connected with national existence, prosperity, and welfare as well as the social order, then the Saemaul Undong is a political movement. Through the spiritual revolution to revitalize the morals of the people, the Saemaul Undong, being a new national spirit, has crystallized its political nature with the establishment of the existentialism to accomplish the national revitalization and the development of Korean democracy through the self-expression of the pan-national movement.

(11) Now let us observe the Saemaul Undong in the light of a new sense of economics. After the Saemaul Undong became a success as a movement of better-living for the people in the rural areas, it moved into a new stage, that is, it became an urban renewal movement as

--- (p. 685) ---

## II. The Spirit of the Saemaui Undong

well as factory Saemaui movement. Through the improvement of environments, the Saemaui Undong has accomplished the inner spiri-tual growth, and, through the spiritual revolution, it launched its effort to enhance economic standards and to improve poor economic conditions,

Thus, the new way of thinking about economics through the Saemaui Undong, overcoming the movement of better-living for an individual, has created a new movement of a better-living for all, and established an atmosphere where every member of the community can live better through diligence, honesty, and cooperation. The idea of the Saemaui Undong in the sense of economics is best seen in communal life, communal prosperity, and communal cooperation.

(12) When we see the Saemaui Undong from a historical point of view, its main objective is the establishment of an ideal welfare-state unparalleled by any other country in the long history of the world. The Korean people who has suffered from many unfavorable incidents such as the manipulation and the division of the country by the great powers, class-discrimination, the indiscriminate influx of foreign culture, shameful grudges that we had to bear, etc.

The historical sense of the Saemaui Undong will alleviate these rancors accumulated in the past, and will implant a new historical sense of peace inherited in diligence, self-help and cooperation. It will also find its true meaning in seeking the main underlying force to build a new nation, a democratic welfare-state; through the expansion of the Saemaui Undong.

(13) If we consider the Saemaui Undong in connection with the sense of our traditional culture, we can easily find the fact that the underly-ing moving force of the spirit of social cooperation already existed in the traditional way of thinking, especially in the idea of the “Ke” and “Hyangyak”, which have a long history of social cooperative tradition. In this respect, the Saemaui Undong has no difference with modernization of the traditional idea, because the “Ke” and “Hyangyak” are exactly the same idea as that of self-help, diligence, and coopera-

--- (p. 686) ---

tion.
(14) When the sense of new education in relation to the Saemaul Undong is considered, the Korean people had been trained under the educational system influenced by foreign culture, but a new educational system born out of the Saemaul Undog which places more emphasis on self-reliance, has been set up and put into force. Thus, the idea of existence emphasizing “here”, the idea of time-reference “now”, and the idea of self-assertion “we” are the result of the new educational goals of the Saemaul Undong. Finally, the Saemaul Undong has created a historical moment where a new image of self-reliant man, a new image of creative man, a new image of cooperative man, and a new image of lively man, can be set up with its mystical power.

### III. Action System of the Saemaul Undong
(1) Among the major factors which contributed to the successful Saemaul Movement, its organization has played the most important role. In this light this chapter will analyze the whole program action system of the movement.
The managerial function of the organization will be examined and described, focusing upon its function of structure in connection with various aspects of the Saemaul Undong such as human and material resources, technology, information, etc.
Before entering into organizational analysis, there will be presented a frame-work, within which the organization is described. In other words, the action system of the movement could be described by dividing it into the operations system and the program structure for the purpose of affording a better understanding. And it should be noted that the operations system could be further divided into a motivation system and program action system, and the program structure, into various kinds and levels of the program.
In addition, the analysis of the action system according to its characteristics will contribute to a better understanding of the whole system. Its characteristics can be defined to be ① integrated, ②

--- (p. 687) ---

## III. Action System of the Saemaul Undong

pan-governmental, and ③ long-standing. Finally the action system can also be divided into a ① program development system, ② program operation system, ③ support system, and ④ public liaison system.

(2) Within the above-mentioned framework, this chapter will describe the nature and characteristics of program development and program operation systems of the action program for individual Saemaul programs, and finally the problems intrinsic in the action program itself.

First of all, the program development system plans and controls business projects, performing the function of a so-called conventional administrative system, and the results of its functions are to be transmitted to the operations system. The various levels of consultative meetings and committees perform functions equivalent to those of the program development system, and their respective organizational structures and functions will be described in detail. They are ① central consultative meetings, ② city or provincial consultative meetings, ③ city or county consultative meetings, ④ “eub” or “myon” consultative meetings, and ⑤ “li” or “dong” consultative meetings.

Let us proceed to the description of the program operations system. This system operates and manages the business planned by the program development system. And its role is to contribute to better planning by feeding back the results of the assistance provided by the program development system. In other words, its functions are divided and analyzed into two types: functions to be performed in the process of receiving support, and those to be performed in the process of feeding back the results. The functions performed in the receiving or transmission process are ① training for the Saemaul Movement, ② publicity of the Saemaul Movement, ③ administrative guidance, ④ material support, ⑤ technical assistance, and so on; and those in the feed-back process are ① confirmation and analysis of the general situation and ② its evaluation by public officials on duty.

Prior to the description of the program operations, the organizational

--- (p. 688) ---

changes of central and local governments will be glanced through, in view of the fact the program operations system, in fact, has been operated under the strong influence of the organizational system of the Home Ministry administration. For example, in accordance with the Presidential Decree 5755 issued on August 19, 1971, the “Development Section” of the Local Bureau was abolished and there were established the offices of “Director of Rural Development,” and “Director of Housing Improvement,” which assumed full charge of the Saemaul Undong for the first time. But these newly established offices also underwent changes as the Saemaul programs went through changes.

(3) As for the description of the action system for the implementation of individual Saemaul programs, primary emphasis was placed on program structure. The sub-divisions of action system for such programs are: ① production basis program, ② income increase program, ③ welfare program, ④ spiritual enlightenment program, ⑤ factory Saemaul Undong, ⑥ and urban Saemaul Undong.
Several ministries take part in the Saemaul programs. Therefore it naturally follows that the Saemaul Undong cannot be concerned only with the tasks and goals of a certain ministry or an institution, but it should rather incorporate into unified Saemaul programs in coordination with various ministries which have to do with the Saemaul Undong. Some of the programs used to be carried out separately by the ministries concerned had to be transferred to the Saemaul programs, since the nature of such programs were more Saemaul-oriented. It is worthwhile to point out that the structure of Saemaul programs are divided on the basis of three criteria: characteristics of a program, the ministry or the agency in charge of a program, and the level of development of the village concerned.

(4) The action system of the Saemaul Undong which we have surveyed from different angles up to now has many characteristics and problems. The problems, most of which resulted from inappropriate conditions, should be taken into consideration in planning future programs and their solutions will lend great assistance for future Saemaul programs. Let us enumerate the problems.

--- (p. 689) ---

## Ⅲ. Action System of the Saemaul Undong

1.  Fundamental in carrying on the Saemaul Undong is voluntary participation. That is, villagers should take part not only in planning programs but also in carrying them out, of their own accord. But the present conditions do not favor voluntary participation in many cases thus contributing to a forced and standardized organizational structure. But this does not necessarily mean that the structure is outdated.
2.  As the Saemaul Undong spreads to more and more parts of the country and its extent gets broader, more ministries and governmental agencies get involved in the movement. But the coordination and cooperation among governmental agencies and ministries concerned are not always satisfactory.
3.  Granted that the complexity of the organizational operations system is inevitable because of the proliferation of the movement, the working-level organizations with limited human resources and ability, when loaded with complex and burdensome tasks imposed by central government, tend to be inefficient and unproductive.
4.  The organization of the Saemaul Undong is multiple-branched, that is, it is branched according to functions and even according to items of business, as seen in the program structure. Such multiple-branching, though unpreventable to some extent in order to make most of the organizational characteristics, is not desirable without an increase in personnel. It would be better-advised to make the most use of the existing organizations rather than to establish new ones.
5.  The action system of the movement in the Home Ministry is comparatively well organized. But those of other ministries are not in good shape. That of the Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries is branched into too many programs.
6.  Any organization in name only is of no use. For example, village development committees should exercise general control over each organization for each program, but actually they do not always perform their proper functions.
7.  Because most of the organizations for certain programs are hierarchically organized according to laws, administrative orders or directions, the members are not well tied together and the inhabitants

--- (p. 690) ---

tend to be indifferent.
⑧ The Saemaul Undong should shake off the simple-minded idea that a group of people can form an organization and father a project. An organization should be evaluated, not by its physical appearance, but by how it perform its proper managerial functions such as planning, coordination, and assessment on the basis of voluntary participation of its members. An organization, which does not discharge its proper functions or whose members do not even know where they belong, is not an organization but in name only. But unfortunately some of the organizations of the Saemaul Undong do not live up to their names.
(5) In view of the above-mentioned problems, the action system of the Saemaul Undong should be adapted to future programs of the movement. In other words, to usher in another successful decade, the action strategies should be readjusted and the action system should be reorganized. Up to now the action system has been controlled mainly by government, and encouraged by late President Park’s devoted interest in the movement. But now that the movement stands on a firm basis, the future action system should be based on grassroots' participation. A reorganization of the action system should take into consideration the fact that its premise is experiencing change. In other words, higher productivity, larger income and better living conditions have been the first concern of the system and its organizations have been organised and managed in such a way as to improve the quality of both material and spiritual life. The slogan of welfare was much publicized but has never materialized satisfactorily. One of the greatest problems facing the Saemaul Undong is how to carve out a future action system which will help to insure satisfactory hygiene, public health, recreation, education, employment, and so on, in the rural area.
Many other ideas will be suggested in the concluding part. The lesson we got from the 10 years’ history of the Saemaul Undong is that though any organization should not be overbearing, our goal under the present circumstances should be to achieve such kind of

--- (p. 691) ---

organization that can work out "production and satisfaction."

## IV. The Rural Saemaul Undong

### (1) Background of the Rural Saemaul Undong

The rural community of Korea originally had been poverty-stricken.
To make matters worse, in the 1960s, while industry made a remark-
able progress, agriculture marked time. This helped to widen the
economic, social and cultural gap between urban and rural communi-
ties. The situation seemed to get worse, and, if left unsettled, threat-
ened to bring forth a double social structure of wealth in the urban
area and poverty in the rural community, which in turn would contri-
bute to greater social instability. More and more people realized and
asserted that the rural community which was lagging behind should be
developed and that no self-sufficient economy would be possible with-
out agricultural development. To meet such requirements of the times,
the late President Park Chung-hee launched the Saemaul Undong as
a rural development movement.

### (2) The Significance and Goal of the Movement

The rural Saemaul Undong was dedicated to the cause that rural
inhabitants should be able to enjoy comfortable living conditions such
as better income, mutual help, richer and modernized and dignified
cultural life, etc.
Underlying the movement were activism and practical philosophy,
because it was well understood that strong will alone, unless it is fol-
lowed by practice, does not guarantee a better life.
In fact, the rural Saemaul Undong was of great significance in
many ways. First, in terms of its composition, it was a movement for
a better life, mainly composed of, and led by, the farming population.
Second, in terms of its programs, it was a movement to improve
living conditions and to lay the foundations of higher productivity.
Third, in terms of public participation in the movement, it was a
movement which contributed to the reformation in villager's way of

--- (p. 692) ---

thinking and in rural development.
The goal of the movement was ① to achieve spiritual enlightenment featured by diligence, self-help and cooperation, ② to achieve higher productivity, ③ to improve rural circumstances, and ④ to bring about technological revolution in agriculture.
In order to obtain these goals, the "10 years" period from 1971 to 1981 is divided into three phases; the first phase for laying a foundation (from 1971 to 1973), the second phase for self-helping development (from 1974 to 1976), and the third phase for achieving self-sufficiency (from 1977 to 1981).

### (3) Motivation and Actions Taken for the Movement

The rural 새마을운동(運動) was launched in 1976 at 33,267 리(里) and 동(洞), each of which was supplied with 335 bags of cement, under the motto that "easy life with no hard work means indolence; dependence with no self-help is nothing more than subordination; society in which no cooperation can be found cannot expect any productivity but will only drive into factional strife."
Each village tentatively launched so-called "10 improvement programs," among which were included widening the road leading to a village, putting small reservoirs in better condition, constructing storages of compost heaps, and so on. But the results reaped in the programs were much better than expected, infusing authorities and officials concerned and villagers with new hope and courage.
Encouraged by the results, the government set short and long range objectives, and set up plans to implement them. For successful implementation of these programs, villages were classified into several types according to their level of development and characteristics.
In 1973, all the villages in the country were divided into three types according to their level of development; basic villages, self-help villages and self-sufficient (or self-reliant) villages, because programs suitable to the level of a village were necessary.
Along with these classifications, the 새마을(Saemaul) programs were classified into primary programs, support programs, and income generating

--- (p. 693) ---

## IV. The Rural Saemaul Undong

programs according to their functions and effects, so as to provide villages with suitable and necessary support.

Meanwhile there were set up standardized programs for each level of villages. The standardized programs for basic villages were mainly new village programs such as street-widening, roofing improvement, maintenance of the dams of streams, and so on. The government provided 500 bags of cement and a ton of reinforcing iron rods to support the programs.

The standardized programs for self-help villages were, besides new village programs, job-producing programs, tree nursery programs, and programs for raising village funds of 50 million won to finance the Saemaul programs. In short, the programs for self-help villages were designed to increase income of the farming population by means of subsidiary projects.

The self-help villages, when they successfully complete their programs, develop into self-sufficient villages. The standardized programs for the self-sufficient villages were programs for laying foundations of productivity, income-wise programs, programs for cooperative production, and so on. For the successful implementation of the programs, a campaign to raise funds of more than 1 million won was launched at the same time. In short, a village which reached the level of self-sufficiency concentrated on income-wise programs and culture and welfare programs.

But it was not always desirable to confine certain standardized programs to certain level of villages. Therefore the standardized programs for each level of villages were mainly suggested as exemplary programs.

### (4) Classification of Villages According to the Conditions of their Location and Their Upgrading

In the previous section, rural villages were classified according to the level of their development. They are also classified into 5 types according to the conditions of their location: plain villages, intermed-iary villages, mountain villages, fishing villages, and suburban villages.

--- (p. 694) ---

The aim of the classification was to contribute to the development of the rural villages by characterizing them on the basis of their geographical conditions, their historical background, and their social and cultural conditions.

8,104 villages were selected as plain villages. The major guided programs for the villages were those for farmland readjustment, establishment of agricultural appliances centers, establishment of farm product processing factories, and so on. 18,895 villages were to be developed into specialized agricultural villages and their major guided programs were those for the semi-livestock industry, development of specialized crops, fuel forestry, and so on.

Business projects were also set up for intensive development of gardening, fruit trees, vegetables, and domestic manual industry in 4,330 suburban villages; in 1,583 fishing villages, modernization of fishing facilities was a major program; and lastly in 1,953 mountain villages, projects for the development of forest resources were undertaken.

Of course the village development plan on the basis of geographical conditions was part of the long-term development plan.

### (5) Higher Income and Higher Agricultural Productivity
Ever since it was launched in 1970, the Saemaul Undong successfully fulfilled its initial experimental programs and it was established on a solid foundation by the middle of the 1970s. By that time, the movement had concentrated mainly on income generating business projects and programs to raise the self-reliance posture of rural villages.

Income generating programs mainly consisted of those for forming main producing area of economical crops, improved distribution of farm produces, expansion of farm produces processing facilities, and forestation. In order to help build self-sufficient villages, special emphasis was put on the cultivation of a self-help spirit of the farming population and the establishment of an independent development system.

### (6) Community Development and Characterization
By the middle of the 1970s, the rural Saemaul Undong embarked

--- (p. 695) ---

# V. The Saemaul Undong in the City, Factory, and School

upon new village infrastructure renovation programs on the basis of past achievements, which involved the modernization of farm houses and their surroundings, which had been carried out at random.
The old villages were reshaped in such a way as to help modernization of agricultural and fishing villages, mechanization of farming, and cooperative farming. And in order to develop rural areas according to their characteristics and to increase side income sources of farm houses; Saemaul factories were distributed to different rural areas.
We have briefly traced the development of the rural Saemaul Undong. It may be safe to say that program planning and actions taken which took into consideration not only the characteristics and level of development of rural villages but also the ability of the farming and fishing population, together with correct judgment on given circumstances and situations, made it possible to achieve the remarkable success of the rural Saemaul Undong, though there were some trial and errors in setting up the program goals and a planning-action system.

## V. The Saemaul Undong in the City, Factory, and School

(1) The industrial development in urban areas in the 1960s and the consequent growth shock necessitated the rural Saemaul Undong which was launched under the slogan of the parallel advance of agriculture and industry. Now, since the Saemaul Undong in rural areas have become established on a solid basis, producing remarkable results, the movement has in turn ushered in the Saemaul Undong in the cities, enterprises, and schools.
In view of the fact that the Saemaul movement was a spiritual support which made possible the prosperity of the 1970s, it is widely believed that the movement will provide the essential driving force to build a democratic welfare state and to realize social justice in the 1980s.
The urban Saemaul Undong, in its first stage, embarked upon

--- (p. 696) ---

various projects in four different places: jobsite, local district, home, and school, with the motto, “diligence, frugality, neighborhood associa-tion, and cooperation.” The movement was successful in programs for urban environment improvement, Saemaul job-producing programs, and education programs for citizens.

In its later stage, the urban Saemaul movement helped not only to establish a sound sense of value based on urbanite’s morality and public good, but also to build up a philosophy of life on the basis of principles and public morals. Various actions were taken to establish an orderly, pure, and dignified urban environment. For example, there were enlightenment efforts to persuade people to obey traffic rules, to pick up waste paper, to use refined language, and to observe good manners.

To infuse the Saemaul spirit in citizens, voluntary participation in the movement by business organizations and other groups, was greatly encouraged. What by holding meetings of neighborhood associations, and what by launching campaigns for orderly streets, fair business dealings, public morality, and ethics, the urban Saemaul Undong led the way in social purification. Through the so-called “three order campaigns” for ① an environmentally pure city, ② physically orderly city, ③ spiritually dignified city, the urban Saemaul Undong was placed on a solid foundation.

(2) In 1980, the emphasis shifted from the three order campaigns to “three civic campaigns”, whose goals are ① to habituate economy in spending, ② to cultivate a law-abiding spirit and ③ to get accustomed to cooperation within the neighborhood. These campaigns cast a good reflection of ① strong will to actively cope with business depression mainly caused by the second oil shock, ② the absolute necessity to reestablish social discipline utterly relaxed following President Park’s assassination on October 26, 1979, ③ the importance of extending a helping hand, and loving care to our poor neighbors.

The factory Saemaul Undong was launched just after the first oil shock near the end of 1973, which dealt a most serious blow to Korean businesses on their way to rapid development.

--- (p. 697) ---

# V. The Saemaul Undong in the City, Factory, and School

The 공장(工場) Saemaul Undong, which started under these unfavorable conditions, was actively carried on to re-arm with the Saemaul spirit the employees who were deeply discouraged by 사업(事業) recession, to cope with the recession, and to overhaul 사업(事業) management systems, under the slogan, “Save materials,” “Energy conservation,” “Better quality of 생산(生産),” and “Higher productivity.”

The action center of the 공장(工場) Saemaul Undong was established by the government. The Saemaul Undong of member enterprises of four economic bodies including the Chamber of Commerce and Industry, concentrated its efforts on planning, investigation, guidance, publicity and education, successfully performing its functions at its stage of 자립(自立) and development.

The outstanding program at the stage was the “working place as second home” movement under the slogan, “Treat the employee as one member of your family; do your job just as your private business.” The movement contributed to better relations between 노동(勞動) and management through giving 공동(共同) birthday parties and operating bride school for employees; and helped to achieve higher productivity.

(3) The second 석유(石油) shock and the Y.H. 무역(貿易) Company 노동(勞動) 파업(罷業) which was one of the greatest 국내(國內) 문제(問題)s in 1979, drove home to the government the importance of the 공장(工場) Saemaul Undong once again.

At the early stage of 자본(資本)주의, the 노사(勞使) 관계는 were taken to be antagonistic, but now at its stage of maturity, it is an indisputable truth that their relations should be improved into 협동(協同) relations through mutual understanding and dialogue.

Above all, on its 정신(精神) side, the 공장(工場) Saemaul Undong helped to establish the cooperative basis of 공동(共同) 경영(經營) by working out the Korean version of business 윤리(倫理); on the 제도(制度)적 side, it helped to improve the channel of 대화(對話) and 협의(協議) by setting up a joint labor-management conference system; and as its future-oriented projects, it is undertaking various programs to ensure 근로(勤勞)자 higher 소득(所得) by introducing Saemaul funds, 공동(共同) commodity purchase and 판매(販賣) system and other Saemaul 사업(事業)s.

--- (p. 698) ---

(4) The school Saemaul movement has been carried on as a form of Saemaul education in that Saemaul as a whole, cannot be perpetuated as a nation-wide campaign without educational support such as spiritual enlightenment and reformation.
That is why the Ministry of Education has steadily carried on Saemaul education so that the whole Saemaul movement might be supported by education and the educational effect might extend to homes, local inhabitants and the whole nation.
Saemaul education has made steady progress. It found its way out of its disarrangement at its inception to its settled phase insuring substantiality not only in school education but also in education of people for higher income and mental culture.
Saemaul education made its way into education promotion policies in the form of promotion of living education, cultivation of cooperation and esprit de corps, building of the local community school or socialization of education. In 1973, Saemaul education became one of the five policies for the promotion of education, representing a very important part of educational activities.
The Saemaul movement which started in the form of a rural Saemaul movement to build up affluent rural villages, has expanded its base until it comprises the urban Saemaul movement, the factory Saemaul movement and finally the school Saemaul movement. In other words, the movement has empirically proved the fact that where there is wisdom and sagacity of our people, there can be launched the Saemaul movement; and it taught us the basic principles of national development.
National development should be a balanced one comprising not only economic growth but also social and cultural development. Such development is possible only when preceded by modernization of human resources. In other words, national modernization programs can be successfully carried out only on the basis of reformation of people’s way of thinking.
It is comparable to a high building built on a solid foundation. That is why we are not envious of Japanese modernization. It deserves

--- (p. 699) ---

# Ⅵ. Saemaul Education

special note that many foreigners who visit Korea are impressed not
by the remarkable economic growth we made during past one decade,
but by the Saemaul spirit with which every citizen is armed.
At this point of time when we are pushing our way toward national development, the tasks we have to take upon ourselves are:
① to get rid of poverty, to build a nation in which both rural and
urban populations live in affluence, ② to establish national discipline
by eliminating injustice and absurdities, and ③ to achieve peaceful
national reunification by consolidating the basis of freedom and democracy. The Saemaul movement is believed to facilitate these tasks to a
great extent. In that conviction, the Saemaul movement in urban areas,
factories and schools is moving in earnest toward its final goal, the
building of a democratic welfare state.

# Ⅵ. Saemaul Education

(1) Saemaul education has both general and historic characteristics.
Just as the education of any nation is influenced by historical and
social circumstances, Saemaul education is no exception.
Let us take a look at the general characteristics of Saemaul education.
One of its most notable characteristics is that it involves every citizen
from the president down to the grass-roots of society. Primarily, every
Korean citizen is called on to participate in the Saemaul education
program regardless of differences in occupation, sex, age, region,
religion, or station in life, and is closely linked with both school and
out of school education.
It takes on a social context in school education by cultivating local
and national patriotism through integrated studies in the form of
social activities, field studies, etc. It can be considered as a life-long
education since every citizen including parents of students participate
in Saemaul education which features a continuing all-time education
in the all-social, all-regional, and all-class aspects.
Secondly, we see it as an effort to revolutionize the human consciousness through arming it with the Saemaul spirit.

--- (p. 700) ---

It is essential and only natural, that Saemaul education initially is conceived as a means to a “better life”, to create a new person, or at least a modern man out of a traditional and poor farmer or urban laborer.

The term “new man” must be defined in relations to both historical and social aspects in view of our reality. The “new man” can be visualized when it stands at the juncture of time and space. It prescribes a profound patriotic sentiment, spirit of national security, implanting democracy in the soil of Korea, historical consciousness of subjecthood, establishment of national ethics, and the creation of modern man indigenous to the Korean idea.

These can be considered urgent historical problems in Korea’s present circumstances, and they are closely related with spiritual education.

The Saemaul spirit is a practical philosophy designed to express and practice the ideals of diligence, self-help, and cooperation. Within the Saemaul spirit the problems of education must be solved in realization that the poverty of the past originated from the lack of a spiritual posture of diligence, self-help, and cooperation. These negative elements cannot serve to contribute to the solution of current social problems facing the nation. It is only feasible when all of our people are armed with the Saemaul spirit.

Lastly, Saemaul education focuses on technical training. It is well-known that modern society is in an age of technical renovation. It is said that the social change of a year today is comparable to that of one thousand years in the past. Therefore, it is clear that it is impossible to build an affluent society, overcome abject poverty, and increase income without adequate agricultural management or construction techniques.

Henceforth, the features of Saemaul education has been on harmonious development of intelligence, virtue, fitness and techniques separate from those having general education characteristics.

It is only common knowledge then that Saemaul education should give priority to technical training in view of the fact that the realization of industrial development, environmental improvement, public

--- (p. 701) ---

# VI. Saemaul Education

hygiene and national self-defense is based upon the study and practice of modern techniques with the backing of modern science.

(2) Let us examine the meaning of Saemaul education. Firstly, Korea’s social education had been isolated for a long time due to rural stagnation and industrial backwardness. It underwent a slight, if not moderate, change towards the end of the 19th century when a group of people conscious of nationalism and a save-the-nation drive rather than a charity motivation launched an unsystematic, unplanned, manual labor industrial style program. It retained its vulnerability, however, under the circumstances of near lack of educational financing or policy vision.

However, Saemaul education in complete contrast to the past in regards to inculcation, is an organized and planned social education for every citizen. This can be construed as the creation of Korea’s life-long education in connection with the idea sponsored by UNESCO since 1965.

Secondly, we can point out wide-range educational objectives as another aspect of Saemaul education. One of the most universal aspects is the decision to involve everyone from students on up to ministers, deputy ministers, officials of every grade, university presidents and deans, professors, lawmakers, judges, prosecutors, business executives, employees, journalists; peasants, housewives, and people from all sectors of society.

This resulted in the education of 28,571,700 persons as of the end of 1979, and financing over 1.94 billion won. This mass social education is unprecedented in history, and it is by no means exaggerated that it is substantially nationwide.

Thirdly, the educational contents and methods of Saemaul education are very characteristic. Spiritual education is common to all cooperative leaders, professors and village women leaders, given at the same time, same place, with the same contents, and by the same instructors. It is not intellectual nor highbrow instruction, but is living and practical based upon everyday experience.

Most characteristic is the “success cases,” and the heroes are the

--- (p. 702) ---

sons and daughters of modest people in general, and they are usually
not well-educated, nor high ranked or well-to-do. Their life style is
extraordinary. Voluntarily participating in the Saemaul education,
motivated by their own desire for a better life and self-consciousness, they present cases of how they had overcome innumerable hardships for themselves and thereby moving the people who listen to their
noble experiences with deep sentiment and who can hardly control the
tears welling up, and thus leading them to reflect on their own lives.
It rises above rank, intellect or occupation, and it is a specific method
of all-human education.
Fourthly, the independent form of Saemaul education is effective
and characteristic, and it is noteworthy that the process of the Sae-
maul movement itself serves as an educational process.
Villagers have established a discussion program among themselves
with a village leader as a pivot where they discuss the village affairs,
small or large, and have cultivated democratic discipline and conscious-
ness concerning responsibilities while solving their own problems.
We might also add the following factors as the results of Saemaul
education: Self-confidence that "we can make it, too", a scientific
processing method, ability to draw a line between public and private
matters, a sense of accomplishments, a coordinating spirit of unity,
and spirit of sacrifice in terms of an educational system.
Fifthly, Saemaul education is not an idle, ideological education, but
an education supported by demonstrative, material evidence such as
income increase and environmental betterment.
The traditional Confucian school of the Yi dynasty was a private,
voluntary institution that served as a source for the establishment of
Confucian ethics. It also cannot be neglected that the night school or
enlightenment movement during Japanese rule played an important role
in terms of educational value. Although education in the past could
attach "head and heart" to the original meaning of education, it failed
to give a "hand" to it. It is very sagacious that Saemaul education
regarded technological education as a part of it, and in view of this,
the ideas on organization of a technical corps is very characteristic

--- (p. 703) ---

## VI. Results of Promotion Projects for Productive Bases

and also unprecedented.
Sixthly, it is highly noteworthy that the Saemaul movement put emphasis on leaders' training in addition to nationwide and all-social education and that it purported to consolidate the “work unit” such as the occupation-unit or rank-unit along with it.
It must also be highly assessed that when specialty is liable to be disregarded according as universality is emphasized, Saemaul education is duly heedful of this respect.

### (3) Let us enumerate the results of Saemaul education.
Firstly, Saemaul education launched a structural innovation of consciousness, and enabled people to conceive the self-confidence that “We can make it, too.” Secondly, Saemaul education is fully justified by the decisive factor that spiritual elements support all material, demonstrative changes. Thirdly, Saemaul education made an effort to achieve a consolidated integrity of technological and workshop education apart from ideology so that it could stimulate the strong will of accomplishment on the part of the people as a working factor for realizing a popular income increase. Fourthly, Saemaul education greatly contributed to the establishment of Korean democracy indigenous to its soil and economic construction, since it has been pragmatically oriented. Fifthly, it is only natural, therefore, that Saemaul education put emphasis on educating people who are able to become Saemaul leaders in order to perpetuate the Saemaul movement.
Saemaul education is in its takeoff stage of ignition, and is taking form in a way indigenous to the Korean soil. It is not without trials and errors, or without problems in its pathway to cope with. But it is valuable for us to cherish with self-confidence that Korea has a promising future, as long as we keep on reflecting on ourselves, cor­recting errors and rounding off the movement.

## VII. Results of Promotion Projects for Productive Bases

### (1) Basic Promotion Projects for Agricultural Production

--- (p. 704) ---

One of the major factors responsible in a large part to the slow development of both rural and fishing villages in some areas was the limitation and low-productiveness due to a poorly established productive base. For that very reason, from our point of view, it is most urgent and significant that something be done to stimulate this relatively stagnant sector by conceiving rural development programs on the basis of a productive promotion project.

This project is designed to stimulate villagers into improving their living surroundings and boosting their incomes with the spirit of furthering extensive production of per unit farming areas, and to be instrumental in drastically raising the productive level, and recruiting lesser labor power and expenditures through modernized management.

The government has thus far conceived and launched the project in the following sectors: ① irrigation development in coping with natural calamities, ② integrated macro-unit agricultural development projects in four river basins along respective watersheds; ③ farm area renewal and drainage improvement for the betterment of agricultural mechanization, and ④ controlling of urbanization envisaged by economic development and utilization of farming areas for other purposes caused by industrialization, along with work on extending farming areas through reclamation of wasteland and drainage on a larger scale.

The nationwide agricultural water facilities amount to 72,000 benefiting 1,121,000 ha of farm land, thus covering 85 per cent of a total of 1,312,000 ha of rice paddy fields as of the end of 1978.

The integrated macro-unit agricultural development project saw the completion of its initial stages in the Keum River, Pyongtaek, Kyongju areas, Keihwado Island and in the Yongsan River as of the end of 1979. The cost to the government was 153.9 billion won, and an area of 69,000 ha was developed.

This unprecedented beneficence on the part of villagers was greeted with the results of an extension of farming area reaching 11,000ha, and farm renewal of 23,000 ha.

The value of the project was the increase of food production of

--- (p. 705) ---

some 135,000 suk 마련되었다. 농업용수(農業用水) 공급(供給)으로 82,000ha의 농지(農地)를 경지정리(耕地整理)함으로써
간접(間接) 성과(成果) of the project are the 농가(農家)의 의식(意識) 전환(轉換) favoring positive and scientific agricultural management.
The government thus helped to develop the human and material growth of the respective areas and to urbanize communities by promoting local tourism.
The 농전(農田) 옥토화(沃土化) 사업(事業) cost the 정부(政府) 1.035 trillion won and realized the renewal of 173,000 ha during the period of 1972 through 1979, thus completing the renewal of 322,000 ha corresponding to 54.8 per cent of the target area of 588,000 ha.
The 직접(直接) 성과(成果) of the project are the 생산성(生産性) 향상(向上) through a high ratio of 토지(土地) 이용률(利用率) and simultaneously, a 생산비(生産費) 절감(節減) effect on production cost through less 노동력(勞動力).
The 간접(間接) 성과(成果); on the other hand, was the 농가(農家) 소득(所得) 증대(増大) aside from 영농(營農) 활동(活動), through an 고용(雇用) 기회(機會) 확대(擴大) during the project period in addition to 농지(農地) 보전(保全) and 시각(視覺) 효과(効果).

## (2) 기본(基本) 진흥(振興) 수산(水産) 생산(生産) 사업(事業)

잦은 자연재해(自然災害) left 어촌(漁村) 피폐(疲弊) and 절망(絶望) and the people remained despondent over their cruel 운명(運命). This was caused largely by the lack of 기초(基礎) 시설(施設), adequate facilities on 어선(漁船) and at 어항(漁港).
It was the 새마을운동(運動), however, in the fishing villages that fought and overcame the 문제(問題) 극복(克服) through motivating a 상부상조(相扶相助) 정신(精神) residing in nation's traditional way of doing things and 사고방식(思考方式), and through 형성 a 협동(協同) 체계(體系) of interdependent loans of “계(契)”, thus helping people 거부(拒否) to submit themselves to the inevitable and the challenges of the vagaries of 자연(自然).
The 새마을운동(運動) in 어촌(漁村) is characterised by the following four sectors; ① 생산(生産) 기반(基盤), ② 소득(所得) 증대(増大)/growth, ③ 복지(福祉) 환경(環境), and ④ 정신(精神) 계몽(啓蒙).
The 생산(生産) 기반(基盤) consists of projects such as the 개선(改善) of

--- (p. 706) ---

fishing ports, cooperative fishing boat construction and the basic establishment of a fishing village interdependent loan system.
From 1972, marking the year of the inception of the fishing village Saemaul movement, through 1979, out of a total expenditure for projects amounting to 25.9 billion won, including that of fishermen, 16.2 billion won, or 63 per cent of the total, was spent for income growth, and 5 billion won, 19 per cent of the total, in the sector of production.
The fishing port improvement project which continued from 1975 through 1979, with a total expenditure of 9,440 million won, repaired 8,361 meters of breakwaters of ports.
Cooperative construction of fishing boats including cooperative operation, cost the government 1.6 billion won, resulting in the construction of 42 new fishing boats.
The basic production facilities project promoted by fishers’ interdependent loans, includes repair work on ferry and loading piers, simple processing and quick repair services.
From 1972 through 1979, the project launched the construction of 418 ferries, 114 quays, 66 loading docks, 50 simple processing plants, 43 breakwaters, 36 commission sales facilities, and 114 other facilities with an investment of 1.6 billion won.

### (3) Saemaul Improvement Project

The Saemaul improvement project in itself is one of the fundamental works, and is characterized by the promotion of productive bases, income increase, and improvement of village surroundings.
The Saemaul improvement project, in connection with the basic promotion of agricultural production, includes forming common compost piles, communal working areas, common stalls, construction of warehouses, repairing riverlets, bridges, and extension of intra-village roads.
The project began in a modest fashion and covered infrastructure and income generating programs, selecting long desired projects first.
In light of this, the Saemaul improvement project played a pivotal role in the Saemaul movement. This has resulted in the overly successful construction of intra-village roads by 65 per cent.

--- (p. 707) ---

## VII. 생산기지(生産基地) 진흥(振興) 사업(事業)의 결과(結果)

교량(橋梁) 건설(建設)은 당초 목표(目標)의 94퍼센트, 공동(共同) 창고(倉庫), 공동(共同) 퇴비(堆肥) 쌓기, 하천피해(河川被害) 복구(復舊) 등은 각각 50퍼센트 이상을 달성(達成)하여 새로운 공동체(共同體) 의식(意識), 근면(勤勉), 자조(自助) 그리고 이상적(理想的) 환경(環境)을 조성(造成)하였다.

마을 주민들은 운동(運動)을 통해 물질적(物質的) 보상(報償)에 비할 수 없는 높은 사기(士氣)를 경험(經驗)하였으며, 이러한 예(例)는 결코 독특(獨特)한 것이 아니다. 수천(數千) 건의 유사(類似) 사례(事例)들은 세계(世界) 어느 국가(國家)에서도 이루어지지 못할 만큼 큰 변화(變化)의 정도(程度)를 보여준다.

⑷ 협동권(協同圈) 개선(改善) 사업(事業)

협동권(協同圈) 개선(改善) 사업(事業)은 마을내(內) 환경(環境)과 생산기지(生産基地)의 공동(共同) 개선(改善)을 대표(代表)한다. 생산기지(生産基地) 진흥(振興) 사업(事業)은 도로(道路)·교량(橋梁) 건설(建設), 하천(河川) 정비(整備), 공동(共同) 창고(倉庫) 설치(設置), 공동(共同) 작업장(作業場) 등으로 분류(分類)된다. 초기(初期) 단계(段階)에서는 새마을운동(새마을運動)이 소규모(小規模) 사업(事業)으로 시작(始作)되어 전체적(全體的)으로 기대(期待) 이상(以上)의 성과(成果)를 거두었다. 이로써 앞으로 더욱 야심찬 사업(事業)으로 이어질 것이라는 기대(期待)를 극적(劇的)으로 부각(浮刻)시켰다.

새마을 개선(改善) 사업(事業)과 협동권(協同圈) 사업(事業)의 차이점(差異點)은 개별(個別) 범위(範圍)에 있는데, 전자는 개별(個別) 마을을 단위(單位)로 하고 후자는 마을내(內)를 단위(單位)로 한다. 따라서 인접(隣接) 마을들은 공동(共同) 관심사(關心事)를 가질 때 마을내(內) 주요(主要) 간선도로(幹線道路)와 관개(灌漑) 시설(施設) 등 상대적(相對的)으로 큰 규모(規模)의 숙원(宿願) 사업(事業)을 착수(着手)한다.

협동권(協同圈) 사업(事業) 중 가장 중요(重要)한 것은 마을내(內) 도로(道路)를 양호(良好)한 상태(狀態)로 유지(維持)하고 새로운 도로(道路)를 개통(開通)하는 것이었다. 이는 예외(例外) 없이 노동(勞動) 생산성(生産性)과 밀접(密接)한 관계(關係)가 있기 때문이다.

둘째, 신설(新設) 도로(道路)와 교량(橋梁)은 생산(生産) 자재(資材) 및 농축산물(農畜産物)의 운반(運搬) 속도(速度)를 높이는 데 기여(寄與)했기 때문에 필수적(必須的)이었다.

정부(政府)는 1974년부터 1979년까지 협동권(協同圈) 사업(事業)에 21억 원을 지원(支援)하였고, 그 결과(結果) 전국(全國) 836개 협동권(協同圈)에서 1,007건의 성공(成功) 사례(事例)를 창출(創出)하였다.

# VIII. Results of Income Growth Projects

## (1) Innovation of Living Style

### ① Progress in the "Revolution with Rising Expectation" and Spiritual Enlightenment.

The most characteristic aspect of the Saemaul movement has been noted as a substantial innovation of the farmers’ conscious structure, the so-called "The Revolution of Rising Expectations".
Through this, they experienced the surprising power of effective energy, of principle, and cooperative work and effective activities through environmental betterment such as extension of intra-village roads and fence mending. They came to realize that it was they who were to blame that they were poor, and that it was feasible for them to work in harmony under the slogans that "We can make it, too," and "we can live a better life through cooperation," cherishing self-confidence, aspirations and expectations. It is analyzed that the "Revolution of Rising Expectations" was mainly led by low-educated farmers rather than the high-educated and became floriferous rapidly.
And the continuous rising of expectation brought about the demand for liberation from the incurring shortage of supply, and there occurred a broader gap between aspirations and realizations, thus inviting mounting dissent and disbelief in the society. Furthermore, the better life movement or income growth movement was overrated in terms of quantitative and material growth, so it cannot be denied that it aggravated the fever of mammonism among farmers.
There emerged therefore the task of renaissance of a national spirit of erasing out excessive expectation and aspirations and also, stamping out spiritual poverty.
